players.product: silicon-photonics foundry services (PH18 SiPho platform) + SiGe drivers/TIAs

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 RESULTS AND Q2 GUIDE (CEO/CFO): Q1 revenue $414 million (+15% YoY vs $358 million), gross profit $111 million (+52% YoY), operating profit $65 million (+96% YoY), net profit $65 million (+62% YoY; 16% net margin vs 11%). Gross margin reached 27% vs a 20% baseline a year earlier, on the CFO's stated linear path toward 39% at the $2.8 billion model (incremental revenue assumed at 59% to gross profit); the CFO agreed ('Yes') when an analyst asked whether the rise came from selling more newer, higher-margin products. Q2 2026 guided to the highest revenue in company history: $455 million ±5% midpoint (+22% YoY, +10% QoQ); management 'strongly reiterate[s]' quarter-over-quarter revenue and margin growth throughout 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $414 million (+15%); gross margin 27%; Q2 guide $455 million ±5% (22% increase YoY, 10% growth QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: SIPHO RAMP: silicon photonics revenue grew 3x year-over-year in Q1 and led the quarter (SiGe +24%, RF SOI +12%, power management +10%, imagers +9% YoY). SiPho production is ramping in FOUR fabs at once - Fab 2 Migdal Haemek, Fab 3 Newport Beach, Fab 9 San Antonio and Fab 7 Uozu (300 mm) - with FIRST-FLOW SiPho revenue shipments from both Fab 2 and Fab 7 in Q1 (Fab 7's first SiPho wafers at 95% yield). 200 Gbps products in a strong ramp for multiple customers. The expansion is on track to grow SiPho capacity FIVE TIMES from the Q4 2025 wafer-shipment base by the end of 2026; in 2027 the focus turns to additional 300 mm capacity in Uozu.
quarterly_data.figure: SiPho revenue 3x year-over-year; Fab 7 first SiPho wafers 95% yield; SiPho capacity five times Q4 2025 base by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CONTRACTED SIPHO DEMAND: long-term photonics customer commitments contractually represent $1.3 billion revenue in 2027 (wafers DELIVERED in 2027), with 'significantly larger valued contracts for 2028', backed by approximately $290 million of prepayments already received from the largest SiPho customers (booked as customer advances and in Q1 operating cash flow). CEO: the $1.3 billion is not those customers' full demand and excludes the broader base of 'more than 50 active SiPho customers'; SiPho was 'somewhere about $230 million' in 2025, and Tower is 'forecasting substantially higher' than $1.3 billion for 2027 SiPho.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.3 billion revenue in 2027 contracted; approximately $290 million in prepayments; more than 50 active SiPho customers

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY / CAPEX AND JAPAN 300MM: the $920 million SiGe + SiPho capacity plan (8-inch fabs in Israel, Newport Beach, Texas plus the 12-inch Uozu fab) is on track - approximately 40% already paid, the remaining 60% to be paid through 2026 and 2027. The TPSCo restructuring moves Tower to FULL OWNERSHIP of 300 mm Fab 7 (Uozu), already profitable at present volumes; with adjacent land Tower expects to scale up to four times current levels (grant-dependent). CEO timeline: METI approval expected very short term, then permits and roughly a year and a half from ground-breaking to tool-in - best case first half of 2028 for that capacity. As an interim step, Tower will place a specific set of tools in the shut-down Arai factory (owned by Nuvoton Winbond) to meet 2027 customer demand; a first phase of Fab 7 SiPho capital spending is approved but not yet quantified (numbers expected within two, three quarters). Separately, a long-term supply agreement with Nuvoton for Fab 5 Tonami keeps 200 mm customers supplied.
quarterly_data.figure: $920 million investment plan, approximately 40% paid, remaining 60% throughout 2026 and 2027; Japan 300 mm up to four times current levels, best case first half of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: FORM-FACTOR TRANSITIONS (CEO): pluggables stay dominant 'at least through the 2030', with Arista-led XPO (extra dense pluggable optics) and NEAR-PACKAGE OPTICS (NPO) emerging next and CPO 'several years down the road'; Tower SiPho was in leading XPO and NPO demos at OFC, has 'multiple design wins' in NPO with 'reasonable volume' shipping in 2026, 2027 and 'strong demand for NPO products in 2027'; NPO is expected to precede a significant CPO ramp for its primary customers. Citing a LightCounting report: SiPho ports go from 30 million (2025) to 137 million (2028) while total ports go from 90 million to 205. CPO investments: in-house 200 mm and 300 mm hybrid bonding with Through-Silicon Vias (SiPho-to-EIC), laser sources incl. DWDM, and compact modulators. Optical circuit switches: partnerships with Salience Labs and Oriole Networks to manufacture SiPho OCS on PH18DA with integrated InP amplifiers; partner Scintil Photonics launched heterogeneously integrated DWDM laser sources for NPO/CPO.
quarterly_data.figure: SiPho ports 30 million (2025) to 137 million (2028) per LightCounting; NPO volume shipping 2026, 2027

quarterly_data.signal: MODULATOR / LASER ROADMAP AND INP CONSTRAINT: demonstrated an all-silicon 400 Gb per lane Mach-Zehnder modulator with Coherent (Coherent's design on Tower's platform); with OpenLight, a heterogeneously integrated 400 Gb per lane InP electro-absorption modulator on PH18DA; moving thin-film lithium niobate toward high volume manufacturing (both side-by-side and chiplet-on-PIC forms, with different customers); organic-polymer modulator partnerships with Lightwave Logic and NLM Photonics. CEO's personal view: TFLN 'will come in fairly strong for one generation' before the industry moves to indium phosphide, which wins on form factor at many channels; integrated lasers are no less reliable than discrete ones, and Tower is agnostic to external vs integrated lasers. INDIUM PHOSPHIDE IS CONSTRAINED - 'the starting material is the constraint' - but Tower says its supply-chain plans position it to meet demand as the integrated InP laser ramps this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 400 Gb per lane modulators (silicon with Coherent; InP with OpenLight); InP starting material constrained

quarterly_data.signal: SIGE ATTACH AND POWER FOR AI RACKS: the SiGe platform sees 'unprecedented demand' for optical-transceiver drivers and TIAs and for active copper cables as a short-reach scale-up alternative to optics; SiGe units go 'pretty much' hand in hand with SiPho units as ports grow, though SiGe revenue grows slower and SiPho earns the higher margin. Power management: Gen3 BCD platform (on-resistance below 1.5 milliohm millimeter squared above 10 V; lead customers saw a 15% reduction in power conversion losses) targets smart power stages and point-of-load converters as AI data center racks move to 800 V DC; 200 mm BCD pricing increased by 13% (a value reset, not a capacity-driven hike, per the CEO).
quarterly_data.figure: SiGe +24% year-over-year; 200 mm BCD pricing increased by 13%; 15% reduction in power conversion losses

quarterly_data.signal: FAB UTILIZATION AND RF SOI: Q1 utilization - Fab 2 around 60% (SiPho and SiGe qualifications continuing), Fab 3 80% (slightly constrained while adding newer SiPho/SiGe processes; expected to rise in Q2), Fab 5 75%, Fab 9 80%, Fab 7 fully utilized, well above the 85% utilization model. 200 mm RF SOI capacity is being repurposed for higher-margin SiPho and SiGe as RF SOI moves to 300 mm; the CEO expects full-year 2026 RF SOI down vs 2025, then record 300 mm RF SOI growth in 2027 and 2028 on design wins for phones first launching in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Fab 2 around 60%, Fab 3 80%, Fab 5 75%, Fab 9 80%, Fab 7 fully utilized, well above 85% utilization model

quarterly_data.signal: MODEL AND COMPETITIVE POSITION (point in time as of this call):the February 2026 model - which already includes all current and future capex - targets $2.8 billion annual revenue, $1.12 billion gross profit, $900 million operating profit and $750 million net profit; the CEO called it a 2028 'midterm' model that excludes the 2027 300 mm SiPho/SiGe expansion and said an update to higher numbers would likely come 'within the next quarters'. On share vs GlobalFoundries/TSMC (analyst framing), the CEO said Tower holds 'by far the leading market share in silicon photonics presently', aims to be the PIC reference design for major integrators (even for TSMC CoWoS-based CPO), and differentiates on III-V and other-material modulation rather than deep digital content; NVIDIA called Tower a development partner in their joint PR. Tax guided to 15%-18% (Q1's 9% included a non-recurring TPSCo benefit).
quarterly_data.figure: February 2026 model: $2.8 billion revenue, $1.12 billion gross profit, $900 million operating profit, $750 million net profit
